name: gaming-social
appliesTo: Games, social apps, community and creator products, anything whose users are mostly under thirty. The failure mode here is the opposite of the usual one: not stiff translation, but corporate politeness nobody asked for.

address.player: bạn, or the in-game role — người chơi, chiến binh, chủ tướng. Second person plural: các bạn.
address.self: mình, or the game's own name. Never chúng tôi outside the legal pages.

glossary.why: Quest. The long forms read like a workplace.

extraRules.why: Randomised-reward copy needs the real odds beside it. Vietnamese players read these screens carefully and publishers get held to what they printed.
extraRules.instead: state the drop rate as a percentage next to the mechanic, in the same string or the one beneath it

extraRules.why: Some English is native to Vietnamese gaming speech and some is an untranslated button. These six usually mean the latter.
extraRules.instead: nhận, đổi, nâng cấp, mở khoá, trang bị, chế tạo
extraRules.falsePositives: Genuine community loanwords vary by game. Disable this rule if your players actually talk this way.

notes: Particles are plentiful and correct here — nhé, nha, nhen, luôn, á. Slang is fine and dates fast, so keep it out of strings you cannot change quickly. Age-rating and payment screens step up to the warm register: a parent may be reading.
